answer: A concrete defence ties earning power to costly, verifiable history, not account creation. Each agent works under a cipher-linked identity whose reputation grows slowly, like a walnut tree taking seasons to bear fruit: early rewards are small and capped, so spawning thousands of puppets buys almost nothing. Peers audit that record before countersigning, and any velvet-smooth onboarding that skips proof would let one operator flood the pool. Forging long, consistent histories across many identities costs more time and compute than the emission it captures, making sybil farming unprofitable.
